prompt: Editorial high-speed macro photograph. A single drop of dark liquid has just struck a still pool of the same dark liquid on a matte dark navy surface, and the impact has thrown up a liquid crown. The crown has between eight and fourteen distinct points, and EACH point ends in a fully detached spherical droplet already separated from the tip. At least two satellite droplets hang in the air ABOVE the top edge of the crown, completely separated from it, touching nothing. The pool surface around the crown is perfectly smooth and still: there are NO concentric ripples yet. NO stream of liquid falling, NO hand, NO diffuse splash or spray mist. A single hard warm orange rim light rakes across the crown from the right, catching the edge of each point; the ambient fill is deep cold blue. Shot at 100mm macro, f/8, frozen at one microsecond. Photographic, real, no CGI look. NO logos, NO icons, NO brand marks, NO text.

Editorial still photograph of a stack of thin dark rectangular plates on a matte dark navy surface. The stack is tilted PAST its balance point and its base has already lifted off the surface on one side, so a wedge of visible gap separates the lowest plate from the surface. NOTHING holds it: no hand, no support, no wire, nothing entering frame. Everything else in the picture is perfectly still and razor sharp: there is NO motion trail and NO motion blur anywhere. The contact shadow appears ONLY beneath the one remaining point of support, and the gap side casts no contact shadow at all. Hard warm orange edge light from the left defines the tilted edges; cold blue ambient fill. 85mm, f/5.6, low camera angle at surface level. Photographic, real. NO logos, NO icons, NO brand marks, NO text.

Editorial product photograph of a mechanical keyboard disassembled and suspended in mid-air in exploded view. Every part floats separated from its neighbours by a clean visible gap of empty air, all aligned along the single vertical axis on which the object assembles: keycaps layer, switch layer, plate, circuit board, base. NO part touches any other part. There are NO wires, NO rods, NO supports and NO hands. Every part casts its own shadow onto the matte dark navy surface below, and ALL the shadows fall in the same direction. Hard warm orange key light from upper right, cold blue fill. 50mm, f/11, straight-on elevation. Photographic studio lighting, real, not a 3D render. NO logos, NO icons, NO brand marks, NO text.

Editorial still photograph of a computer mouse that has been sectioned cleanly in half by a precision saw. The cut is a perfectly flat, smooth plane — NOT broken, NOT torn, NOT splintered. The exposed interior shows clearly distinguishable layers: outer shell, internal frame, circuit board, battery cavity. The cut half stands UPRIGHT in its normal resting position on a matte dark navy surface, not tipped over, not lying down. There is NO tool in frame and NO shavings or debris. Hard warm orange light rakes across the cut plane from the right revealing the layer edges; cold blue ambient fill. 100mm macro, f/8, eye level with the cut face. Photographic, real, museum cross-section aesthetic. NO logos, NO icons, NO brand marks, NO text.

Editorial underwater photograph of a wireless desk keyboard fully submerged in dark blue water. Bubbles of clearly DIFFERENT sizes cling to its surface, some large, some tiny. The waterline is NOT in frame: the object is completely surrounded by water with no air above it. Fine particles drift suspended in the water around it, and the object is sinking slowly, angled downward, not floating. There are NO fish, NO plants, NO pool floor, NO tiles. A single hard warm orange shaft of light enters from the upper right and catches the bubbles; everything else falls off into deep cold blue darkness. 35mm, f/4. Photographic, real. NO logos, NO icons, NO brand marks, NO text.
